text:
hao: Ran a focused tiny-chat soak on host preparse changes. Seeing p95 drift and kvcache churn.

anya: Numbers?

hao: baseline p95 5.1ms -> refactor p95 7.2ms. kvcache hit 93% -> 75% during the run.

sam: Any hotspots?

hao: Flame snippet:

ingress::preparse 38%
http2_writer::writev 15%
memcpy 10%
kvcache::lookup 6%
other 31%

zach: That memcpy + writev combo explains small-write tail. Are we copying per-frame before gRPC?

hao: Yes, parse_layer normalizes chunk boundaries and copies to a contiguous buffer. For tiny frames this is expensive. Also kernel selection is flipping between small/med kernels which reinitializes KV scratch, causing evictions.

anya: Quick mitigations: 1) add kernel-selection hysteresis (require sustained seq_len change), 2) zero-copy proto views to remove the memcpy, 3) adaptive writev coalesce with per-route config.

perf-bot: Commit b7c4d: "ingress: adaptive-writev + kernel-hysteresis" queued for staging bench.

sam: If we do zero-copy, remember buffer lifetime rules; add debug-mode verifier to catch use-after-free.

zach: Also add a tiny-chat harness into CI to catch regressions early.

anya: I'll draft an RFC and canary plan (eng-runtime RFC link in PR). Canary to start: staging -> canary-10pct at 1844450600.

hao: Filed ENGRT-725 for the zero-copy spike and ENGRT-726 for CI harness.

sam: I'll review kernel-hysteresis PR. Thanks all.
